claims.text: The initial hot-pressed ZrB2 components have approximately 90% theoretical density and open surface porosity.
Pressure infiltration of 10 vol% elemental Si at 1450 °C for 1 h under 5 MPa argon will produce a Si-enriched surface layer in ZrB2.
The intervention will create a continuous Si-rich barrier approximately 10 µm thick.
The Si-rich barrier will lower the wettability of ZrB2 by molten aluminum.
The Si-rich barrier will slow dissolution of the underlying ZrB2 in molten aluminum.
The barrier will limit direct contact between molten aluminum and ZrB2.
The barrier will limit intermetallic formation at the molten-aluminum/ZrB2 interface.
Si-infiltrated ZrB2 will exhibit at least a 50% lower corrosion rate than untreated ZrB2 in molten Al–12 wt% Si at 700 °C for 100 h under an inert atmosphere.
Si-infiltrated ZrB2 will show approximately 50% less mass loss than untreated ZrB2 after 100 h.
The intervention will remain effective from 650 to 750 °C for exposure times up to 200 h in an inert atmosphere.
Above 800 °C, the Si barrier may degrade.
The proposed mechanism is inferred from analogous Si-infiltrated boride composites.
The proposed intervention has not yet been directly tested for ZrB2 against molten aluminum.
Untreated ZrB2 exposed under identical conditions is the experimental baseline.
A reduction in mass loss of less than 25% relative to untreated ZrB2, or failure to form a continuous Si-rich layer, is designated as a falsifying result.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires approximately or at least a 50% reduction, but the stated falsification threshold is less than 25%. A measured reduction between 25% and 49% would fail the quantitative prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.
